claim: Wnt5a has been implicated in melanoma progression and metastasis.
source: Wnt5a has been implicated in melanoma progression and metastasis, although the exact downstream signaling events that contribute to melanoma metastasis are poorly understood.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that sets up the research context.

claim: Wnt5a signaling results in APT1 mediated depalmitoylation of CD44 and MCAM, resulting in increased melanoma invasion.
source: Wnt5a signaling results in acyl protein thioesterase 1 (APT1) mediated depalmitoylation of pro-metastatic cell adhesion molecules CD44 and MCAM, resulting in increased melanoma invasion.
evidence: This statement references prior work establishing the relationship between Wnt5a, APT1, and melanoma invasion.

claim: Wnt5a signaling regulates APT1 activity through induction of APT1 phosphorylation.
source: Here, we show Wnt5a signaling regulates APT1 activity through induction of APT1 phosphorylation and we further investigate the functional role of APT1 phosphorylation on its depalmitoylating activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Phosphorylation increased APT1 depalmitoylating activity.
source: We found phosphorylation increased APT1 depalmitoylating activity and reduced APT1 dimerization.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data using the DPP-3 probe and other assays.

claim: Phosphorylation reduced APT1 dimerization.
source: We found phosphorylation increased APT1 depalmitoylating activity and reduced APT1 dimerization.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by size-exclusion chromatography data.

claim: APT1 phosphorylation increases melanoma invasion in vitro.
source: We further determined APT1 phosphorylation increases melanoma invasion in vitro, and also correlated with increased tumor grade and metastasis.
evidence: This is supported by spheroid invasion assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: APT1 phosphorylation correlated with increased tumor grade and metastasis.
source: We further determined APT1 phosphorylation increases melanoma invasion in vitro, and also correlated with increased tumor grade and metastasis.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data on human melanoma tumor arrays.

claim: Inhibition of APT1 may represent a novel way to treat Wnt5a driven cancers.
source: Inhibition of APT1 may represent a novel way to treat Wnt5a driven cancers.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential therapeutic applications based on the findings.

claim: Wnt5a expression is strongly correlated with melanoma progression and metastasis.
source: Wnt5a expression is strongly correlated with melanoma progression and metastasis (Bittner et al., 2000; Carr et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Melanoma has a 5 year survival rate of only 17% for metastatic melanoma patients.
source: Melanoma is the deadliest form of skin cancer, with a 5 year survival rate of only 17% for metastatic melanoma patients (Sandru et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a cited statistic from the literature.

claim: Wnt5a expression is positively correlated with poor outcome, with high Wnt5a expression being associated with decreased patient survival.
source: Importantly, Wnt5a expression is positively correlated with poor outcome, with high Wnt5a expression being associated with decreased patient survival (Da Forno et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Wnt5a expression has been suggested to be used as a prognostic clinical risk factor.
source: With this information, it has been suggested that Wnt5a expression be used as a prognostic clinical risk factor (Da Forno et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Wnt5a signaling promotes migration and invasion in melanoma cells.
source: Our lab and others have shown Wnt5a signaling promotes migration and invasion in melanoma cells (Dissanayake et al., 2007; Wang et al., 2015; Weeraratna et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature including work from the authors' lab.

claim: Wnt5a is a secreted ligand in the noncanonical Wnt signaling pathway.
source: Wnt5a is a secreted ligand in the noncanonical Wnt signaling pathway and upon interacting with its Frizzled receptor, activates a signal transduction cascade (Sato et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Wnt5a supported by a citation.

claim: Wnt5a signaling controls cell polarity and directional cell movement.
source: Wnt5a signaling controls cell polarity and directional cell movement, and Wnt5a treatment promotes recruitment and reorganization of proteins involved in cell adhesion and cell signaling (Witze et al., 2008; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Wnt5a treatment promotes recruitment and reorganization of proteins involved in cell adhesion and cell signaling.
source: Wnt5a signaling controls cell polarity and directional cell movement, and Wnt5a treatment promotes recruitment and reorganization of proteins involved in cell adhesion and cell signaling (Witze et al., 2008; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Wnt5a stimulation promotes asymmetrical localization of cell adhesion molecules.
source: Wnt5a stimulation promotes asymmetrical localization of cell adhesion molecules, increases cell motility, and elevates levels of free Ca2+ to induce Ca2+ signaling in a polarized manner (Witze et al., 2008; Witze et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Wnt5a stimulation increases cell motility.
source: Wnt5a stimulation promotes asymmetrical localization of cell adhesion molecules, increases cell motility, and elevates levels of free Ca2+ to induce Ca2+ signaling in a polarized manner (Witze et al., 2008; Witze et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Wnt5a stimulation elevates levels of free Ca2+ to induce Ca2+ signaling in a polarized manner.
source: Wnt5a stimulation promotes asymmetrical localization of cell adhesion molecules, increases cell motility, and elevates levels of free Ca2+ to induce Ca2+ signaling in a polarized manner (Witze et al., 2008; Witze et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The tyrosine kinase receptor ROR2 is predominantly expressed in metastatic melanoma.
source: The tyrosine kinase receptor ROR2, which is predominantly expressed in metastatic melanoma, has been shown to specifically interact with Wnt5a and mediate Wnt5a signaling (O'Connell et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: ROR2 has been shown to specifically interact with Wnt5a and mediate Wnt5a signaling.
source: The tyrosine kinase receptor ROR2, which is predominantly expressed in metastatic melanoma, has been shown to specifically interact with Wnt5a and mediate Wnt5a signaling (O'Connell et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Elevated Wnt5a expression promotes melanoma invasion.
source: In addition to reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton and polarized localization of cell adhesion molecules, others have shown that elevated Wnt5a expression promotes melanoma invasion and human biopsies directly correlated Wnt5a expression with tumor grade (Weeraratna et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Human biopsies directly correlated Wnt5a expression with tumor grade.
source: In addition to reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton and polarized localization of cell adhesion molecules, others have shown that elevated Wnt5a expression promotes melanoma invasion and human biopsies directly correlated Wnt5a expression with tumor grade (Weeraratna et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: CD44 levels are elevated in multiple cancer types.
source: CD44 levels are elevated in multiple cancer types and MCAM is expressed in melanoma cells and not untransformed melanocytes (Wielenga et al., 1993; Shih et al., 1994a; Shih et al., 1994b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: MCAM is expressed in melanoma cells and not untransformed melanocytes.
source: CD44 levels are elevated in multiple cancer types and MCAM is expressed in melanoma cells and not untransformed melanocytes (Wielenga et al., 1993; Shih et al., 1994a; Shih et al., 1994b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: CD44 has been shown to be palmitoylated.
source: CD44 has been shown to be palmitoylated and inhibiting CD44 palmitoylation through cysteine point mutations strongly enhanced breast cancer migration (Babina et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Inhibiting CD44 palmitoylation through cysteine point mutations strongly enhanced breast cancer migration.
source: CD44 has been shown to be palmitoylated and inhibiting CD44 palmitoylation through cysteine point mutations strongly enhanced breast cancer migration (Babina et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Cysteine point mutations that block MCAM palmitoylation increases metastatic cell behavior in melanoma cells both in vitro and in vivo.
source: Similarly, cysteine point mutations that block MCAM palmitoylation increases metastatic cell behavior in melanoma cells both in vitro and in vivo (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: S-Palmitoylation is the reversible addition of a 16-carbon fatty acid to cysteine residues via a thioester linkage.
source: S-Palmitoylation is the reversible addition of a 16-carbon fatty acid to cysteine residues via a thioester linkage.
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge about palmitoylation.

claim: Palmitate addition is mediated by palmitoyltransferases.
source: Palmitate addition is mediated by palmitoyltransferases and acyl protein thioesterases (APTs) remove palmitate from proteins to regulate protein localization, trafficking, and cell signaling (Vartak et al., 2014; Linder and Deschenes, 2007; Lin and Conibear, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Acyl protein thioesterases (APTs) remove palmitate from proteins to regulate protein localization, trafficking, and cell signaling.
source: Palmitate addition is mediated by palmitoyltransferases and acyl protein thioesterases (APTs) remove palmitate from proteins to regulate protein localization, trafficking, and cell signaling (Vartak et al., 2014; Linder and Deschenes, 2007; Lin and Conibear, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Wnt5a stimulation has been shown to induce the depalmitoylation of both MCAM and CD44 through APT1.
source: Wnt5a stimulation has been shown to induce the depalmitoylation of both MCAM and CD44 through APT1 (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Wnt5a mediated melanoma cell invasion is reduced by treatment with a small molecule inhibitor of APT proteins.
source: Wnt5a mediated melanoma cell invasion is reduced by treatment with a small molecule inhibitor of APT proteins.
evidence: This statement references prior work on APT inhibitors.

claim: Growth factor stimulation is sufficient to inhibit depalmitoylating activity of APT proteins.
source: Another group has also shown that growth factor stimulation is also sufficient to inhibit depalmitoylating activity of APT proteins (Kathayat et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Increased APT1 expression increased melanoma invasion in the absence of exogenous Wnt5a.
source: Wang, et al. demonstrated that increased APT1 expression increased melanoma invasion in the absence of exogenous Wnt5a (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The only phosphorylation sites identified on APT1 were on serine residues 209 and 210.
source: The only phosphorylation sites identified on APT1 were on serine residues 209 and 210.
evidence: This is a primary finding from mass spectrometry analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Single phosphorylation of either serine 209 or 210 was detected.
source: Whereas single phosphorylation of either serine 209 or 210 was detected, we can't rule out the possibility of dual phosphorylation (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: A previous high throughput mass spectrometry screen identified APT1 phosphorylation on serine residues 209 and 210 in laryngeal cancer cells.
source: These findings are consistent with a previous high throughput mass spectrometry screen by another group that identified APT1 phosphorylation on serine residues 209 and 210 in laryngeal cancer cells (Phosphosite.org, site group ID: 25299324 and 25299327).
evidence: This statement references a database entry from prior work.

claim: Wnt5a stimulation increases phosphorylated APT1 detected with antibodies to pS209-APT1 and pS210-APT1.
source: With phospho-APT1 antibodies to both serine 209 and serine 210, we detected phosphorylated APT1 (pS209-APT1/pS210-APT1) that increased following Wnt5a stimulation (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The induction of APT1 phosphorylation at Ser210 was detected in whole cell lysate without immunoprecipitation.
source: The induction of APT1 phosphorylation at Ser210 was detected in whole cell lysate without immunoprecipitation, showing a relatively high stoichiometry of phosphorylated APT1 to total APT1 after Wnt5a stimulation (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: APT1 phosphorylation peaked at 30 min and began to decrease at 60 min.
source: APT1 phosphorylation peaked at 30 min and began to decrease at 60 min (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by time course data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: When WM239A cells expressing APT1SA are treated with Wnt5a, the levels of phosphorylation of APT1 at Ser209 were unchanged compared to cells expressing APT1WT.
source: When WM239A cells ectopically expressing APT1SA are treated with Wnt5a, the levels of phosphorylation of APT1 at Ser209 measured by immunoblotting were unchanged compared to cells expressing APT1WT (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The phosphorylated serine residues 209 and 210 are solvent exposed on the lip of the hydrophobic putative acyl-binding channel and adjacent to the catalytic triad.
source: We found that the phosphorylated serine residues 209 and 210 are solvent exposed on the lip of the hydrophobic putative acyl-binding channel and adjacent to the catalytic triad (Ser119, His208, Asp174), suggesting phosphorylation of these sites could influence APT1 activity (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is based on structural modeling shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Phosphorylation of serine 209 and 210 could influence APT1 activity.
source: We found that the phosphorylated serine residues 209 and 210 are solvent exposed on the lip of the hydrophobic putative acyl-binding channel and adjacent to the catalytic triad (Ser119, His208, Asp174), suggesting phosphorylation of these sites could influence APT1 activity (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural position of the phosphorylation sites.

claim: APT1S209D has increased depalmitoylating activity compared to APT1WT.
source: APT1S209D was found to have increased depalmitoylating activity compared to APT1WT (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro fluorescence assay data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: APT1S119A generated minimal fluorescence throughout the duration of the assay.
source: A catalytically inactive mutant where catalytic serine 119 is mutated to alanine (referred to as APT1S119A) was used as a negative control and generated minimal fluorescence throughout the duration of the assay (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro fluorescence assay data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Higher initial velocities were measured for APT1S209D at each substrate concentration compared to APT1WT.
source: We measured higher initial velocities for APT1S209D at each substrate concentration compared to APT1WT (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by enzyme kinetics data shown in Table 1.

claim: Wnt5a stimulation significantly increased the fluorescence emission compared to control buffer treated cells, indicating an increase in endogenous APT1 activity.
source: We quantified fluorescence emission in individual cells and determined that Wnt5a stimulation significantly increased the fluorescence emission compared to control buffer treated cells, indicating an increase in endogenous APT1 activity (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by live-cell microscopy data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: APT1 isolated from Wnt5a stimulated cells showed an increase in depalmitoylating activity compared to untreated control.
source: APT1 isolated from Wnt5a stimulated cells showed an increase in depalmitoylating activity compared to untreated control (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro fluorescence assay data on immunoprecipitated APT1.

claim: Stimulation with the canonical Wnt ligand, Wnt3a, was unable to increase APT1 activity compared to Wnt5a.
source: While the non-canonical Wnt ligand Wnt5a is sufficient to increase APT1 activity we found stimulation with the canonical Wnt ligand, Wnt3a, was unable to increase APT1 activity compared to Wnt5a and was similar to cells treated with control buffer (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by live-cell microscopy data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The ability to increase APT1 activity appears to be specific to the non-canonical Wnt pathway.
source: Therefore, the ability to increase APT1 activity appears to be specific to the non-canonical Wnt pathway.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential effects of Wnt5a and Wnt3a on APT1 activity.

claim: APT1S209D has greater depalmitoylating activity in cells compared to either APT1WT or APT1SA.
source: Consistent with the in vitro results, APT1S209D has greater depalmitoylating activity in cells compared to either APT1WT or APT1SA (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by live-cell microscopy data shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Wnt5a treatment increases APT1WT activity to levels higher than the phosphomimetic mutant APT1S209D.
source: Wnt5a treatment increases APT1WT activity to levels higher than the phosphomimetic mutant APT1S209D.
evidence: This is based on live-cell microscopy data comparing Wnt5a-treated APT1WT to untreated APT1S209D.

claim: Wnt5a stimulation is unable to increase activity of phospho-dead APT1SA.
source: As expected Wnt5a stimulation is unable to increase activity of phospho-dead APT1SA or further increase the constitutive elevated activity of APT1S209D (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by live-cell microscopy data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Wnt5a stimulation is unable to further increase the constitutive elevated activity of APT1S209D.
source: As expected Wnt5a stimulation is unable to increase activity of phospho-dead APT1SA or further increase the constitutive elevated activity of APT1S209D (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by live-cell microscopy data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Treatment with either protein kinase inhibitors inhibited the Wnt5a mediated increase in APT1 activity to levels comparable to unstimulated cells.
source: Treatment with either protein kinase inhibitors inhibited the Wnt5a mediated increase in APT1 activity to levels comparable to unstimulated cells (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by live-cell microscopy data with kinase inhibitors shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Phosphorylation of APT1 is a main driver of increased APT1 activity in response to Wnt5a.
source: These results suggest that phosphorylation of APT1 is a main driver of increased APT1 activity in response to Wnt5a.
evidence: This is an inference based on the kinase inhibitor experiments and phospho-mutant data.

claim: Cells produced similar amounts of wild type and mutant APT1 protein.
source: We found cells produced similar amounts of wild type and mutant APT1 protein (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: MCAM palmitoylation was highest in APT1SA samples, indicating a decreased ability to depalmitoylate MCAM.
source: We found MCAM palmitoylation to be highest in APT1SA samples, indicating a decreased ability to depalmitoylate MCAM (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by acyl biotin exchange assay data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The APT1S209D sample had the lowest level of palmitoylated MCAM, indicating the highest level of depalmitoylating activity.
source: In contrast, the APT1S209D sample had the lowest level of palmitoylated MCAM, indicating the highest level of depalmitoylating activity.
evidence: This is supported by acyl biotin exchange assay data.

claim: The phosphorylation state of APT1 regulates depalmitoylation of endogenous substrates.
source: These data serve as evidence that the phosphorylation state of APT1 regulates depalmitoylation of endogenous substrates.
evidence: This is an inference based on the MCAM palmitoylation data with APT1 phospho-mutants.

claim: Expression of APT1SA resulted in decreased invasion, similar to the negative control CFP.
source: We found that expression of APT1SA resulted in decreased invasion, similar to the negative control CFP, while APT1S209D significantly increased melanoma invasion (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is supported by spheroid invasion assay data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: APT1S209D significantly increased melanoma invasion.
source: We found that expression of APT1SA resulted in decreased invasion, similar to the negative control CFP, while APT1S209D significantly increased melanoma invasion (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is supported by spheroid invasion assay data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: When the activity of APT1 is inhibited with the selective inhibitor ML348, invasion is blocked.
source: When the activity of APT1 is inhibited with the selective inhibitor ML348, invasion is blocked, demonstrating the increased invasion observed in cells expressing APT1S209D is mediated by APT1 activity (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by spheroid invasion assay data with ML348 shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The increased invasion observed in cells expressing APT1S209D is mediated by APT1 activity.
source: When the activity of APT1 is inhibited with the selective inhibitor ML348, invasion is blocked, demonstrating the increased invasion observed in cells expressing APT1S209D is mediated by APT1 activity (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is an inference based on the ML348 inhibitor data.

claim: Phosphorylation of Ser209 increases depalmitoylating activity in cells, in turn increasing metastatic cell behavior.
source: Together these results indicate phosphorylation of Ser209 increases depalmitoylating activity in cells, in turn increasing metastatic cell behavior.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined data from activity assays and invasion assays.

claim: Each APT1 mutant possessed similar thermostability to that of APT1WT.
source: We found that each mutant possessed similar thermostability to that of APT1WT, indicating that the point mutations are not destabilizing the folding of the protein (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by differential scanning fluorimetry data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The point mutations are not destabilizing the folding of the protein.
source: We found that each mutant possessed similar thermostability to that of APT1WT, indicating that the point mutations are not destabilizing the folding of the protein (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is an inference based on the thermostability data.

claim: Previous crystal structures of APT1 revealed a weak asymmetric dimer in which the active site was occluded by the dimer interface, suggestive of an inactive dimer.
source: Previous crystal structures of APT1 revealed a weak asymmetric dimer in which the active site was occluded by the dimer interface, suggestive of an inactive dimer (Devedjiev et al., 2000; Won et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior structural studies.

claim: The phosphorylation sites 209 and 210 reside in the interface of the dimer.
source: Our interrogation of the crystal structure revealed that the phosphorylation sites 209 and 210 reside in the interface of the dimer and could potentially destabilize the dimeric form and decrease the inhibitory dimeric interaction.
evidence: This is based on structural modeling of the crystal structure.

claim: Phosphorylation sites 209 and 210 could potentially destabilize the dimeric form and decrease the inhibitory dimeric interaction.
source: Our interrogation of the crystal structure revealed that the phosphorylation sites 209 and 210 reside in the interface of the dimer and could potentially destabilize the dimeric form and decrease the inhibitory dimeric interaction.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the structural position of the phosphorylation sites.

claim: The distance between the serine residues to the methionine (Met 65) residue on the opposite dimer is less than 4 Å.
source: We measured the distance between the serine residues to the methionine (Met 65) residue on the opposite dimer and found a short distance of less than 4 Å (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is based on structural modeling shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Phosphorylation of one of these sites would be less favorable for dimer formation.
source: We therefore hypothesized that phosphorylation of one of these sites would be less favorable for dimer formation.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the structural proximity of the phosphorylation sites to the dimer interface.

claim: When APT1 was loaded on the column at a concentration of 0.1 mg/ml both APT1WT and APT1S209D eluted at the same time as a 29kD standard.
source: When APT1 was loaded on the column at a concentration of 0.1 mg/ml both APT1WT and APT1S209D eluted at the same time as a 29kD standard.
evidence: This is supported by size-exclusion chromatography data.

claim: When the protein concentration is increased to 0.25 mg/ml a second peak of APT1WT begins to resolve closer to the 44kD standard.
source: When the protein concentration is increased to 0.25 mg/ml a second peak of APT1WT begins to resolve closer to the 44kD standard (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by size-exclusion chromatography data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: When the APT1WT protein concentration was increased to 0.375 mg/ml a second peak was resolved near the 44kD standard that was not observed with APT1S209D.
source: When the APT1WT protein concentration was increased to 0.375 mg/ml a second peak was resolved near the 44kD standard that was not observed with APT1S209D.
evidence: This is supported by size-exclusion chromatography data.

claim: The peak at 29kD for APT1WT is abolished at 0.375 mg/ml concentration.
source: Additionally, the peak at 29kD for APT1WT is abolished at this concentration (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by size-exclusion chromatography data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: APT1 dimerizes and phosphorylation of APT1 reduces dimerization.
source: These results support the findings that APT1 dimerizes and phosphorylation of APT1 reduces dimerization.
evidence: This is an inference based on the size-exclusion chromatography data.

claim: The APT1 gene is mutated in multiple tumor types, with the highest frequency of serine 210 mutated specifically to a leucine.
source: The APT1 gene is mutated in multiple tumor types, with the highest frequency of serine 210 mutated specifically to a leucine (Figure 5A) (Gao et al., 2013 and Cerami et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to cancer genomics databases and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: APT1S210L exhibits an almost identical increase in activity to the phospho-mimetic APT1S209D.
source: When we compare the depalmitoylating activity of APT1S210L to APT1S209D, we find that S210L exhibits an almost identical increase in activity to the phospho-mimetic APT1S209D (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro fluorescence assay data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Similar inhibition of APT1 depalmitoylation by ML348 was observed using the DPP-3 probe as a substrate for APT1S209D and APT1S210L.
source: We also observe similar inhibition of APT1 depalmitoylation by ML348 using the DPP-3 probe as a substrate for APT1S209D and APT1S210L (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro fluorescence assay data with ML348 shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: A leucine at position 210 is located 5.5 Å from the methionine of the adjacent APT1 monomer.
source: To visualize how a S210L mutation would affect dimerization, we modeled the substitution on the three-dimensional crystal structure and determined a leucine at position 210 is located 5.5 Å from the methionine of the adjacent APT1 monomer (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is based on structural modeling shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Steric hindrance disrupts the dimerization of APT1 when leucine is at position 210.
source: With a neutral charge leucine positioned a small distance from the dimer interface, we propose steric hindrance disrupts the dimerization of APT1.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the structural modeling of the S210L mutation.

claim: Expression of APT1S210L increased melanoma invasion when compared to APT1WT and negative control CFP.
source: Expression of APT1S210L increased melanoma invasion when compared to APT1WT and negative control CFP (Figure 5D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by spheroid invasion assay data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Treating spheroids expressing APT1S210L with ML348 significantly reduces cell invasion.
source: Similar to the phospho-mimetic APT1S209D, treating spheroids expressing APT1S210L with ML348 significantly reduces cell invasion (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by spheroid invasion assay data with ML348 shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: APT1S210L increases metastatic behavior compared to wild type and this is dependent on the catalytic activity of APT1.
source: These results demonstrate that APT1S210L increases metastatic behavior compared to wild type and this is dependent on the catalytic activity of APT1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the invasion assay data with APT1S210L and ML348 inhibitor.

claim: A correlation exists between high pAPT1 staining and increased tumor grade.
source: We discovered a correlation between high pAPT1 staining and increased tumor grade (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data on human melanoma tumor arrays shown in Figure 5E.

claim: High pAPT1 staining correlates with melanoma metastatic samples.
source: When looking at melanoma metastatic samples we observed the same correlation (Figure 5F, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), implicating increased APT1 phosphorylation with increased tumor progression and metastasis.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data on metastatic melanoma samples shown in Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Increased APT1 phosphorylation is implicated with increased tumor progression and metastasis.
source: When looking at melanoma metastatic samples we observed the same correlation (Figure 5F, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), implicating increased APT1 phosphorylation with increased tumor progression and metastasis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the immunohistochemistry data showing correlation between pAPT1 and tumor grade/metastasis.

claim: Wnt5a signaling induces APT1 phosphorylation and this activates APT1, increasing its depalmitoylating activity and thus depalmitoylation of its substrates.
source: Here, we uncover a molecular switch that promotes protein depalmitoylation in response to non-canonical Wnt signaling. We demonstrate Wnt5a signaling induces APT1 phosphorylation and this activates APT1, increasing its depalmitoylating activity and thus depalmitoylation of its substrates.
evidence: This is a summary of the primary findings supported by multiple experiments in the manuscript.

claim: This is the first example of differential phosphorylation of APT1 in response to an extracellular signal.
source: While phosphorylation of these serine residues has been observed in mass spectrometry studies, this is the first example of differential phosphorylation of APT1 in response to an extracellular signal.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: Activation of APT1 signaling results in increased depalmitoylating activity, leading to increased melanoma invasion, and correlating with increased tumor grade and metastasis.
source: Ultimately, activation of APT1 signaling results in increased depalmitoylating activity, leading to increased melanoma invasion, and correlating with increased tumor grade and metastasis.
evidence: This is a summary statement integrating multiple findings from the manuscript.

claim: The phospho-mimetic mutant APT1 has greater thioesterase activity compared to wild type APT1.
source: This assay revealed the phospho-mimetic mutant APT1 has greater thioesterase activity compared to wild type APT1.
evidence: This is supported by the DPP-3 fluorescence assay data.

claim: The phospho-dead mutant had similar activity to wild type APT1.
source: The increase in activity was also observed by live cell imaging and the phospho-dead mutant had similar activity to wild type APT1.
evidence: This is supported by live-cell microscopy data with the DPP-3 probe.

claim: The ability to increase endogenous APT1 activity is specific to Wnt5a and the noncanonical Wnt pathway.
source: Using live imaging, we were able to demonstrate that the ability to increase endogenous APT1 activity is specific to Wnt5a and the noncanonical Wnt pathway, as we found Wnt3a lacks this ability.
evidence: This is supported by live-cell microscopy data comparing Wnt5a and Wnt3a effects.

claim: The dimer must dissociate prior to interaction with its substrate.
source: The first crystal structure of APT1 revealed a dimer with the active site buried in the dimer interface (Devedjiev et al., 2000), suggesting the dimer must dissociate prior to interaction with its substrate.
evidence: This is an inference based on the crystal structure showing the active site is occluded in the dimer.

claim: A complete shift of the APT1WT monomer population to the dimer was detected using size-exclusion chromatography.
source: Using size-exclusion chromatography we detected a complete shift of the APT1WT monomer population to the dimer.
evidence: This is supported by size-exclusion chromatography data.
